new_entities.name: Islet transplantation for type 1 diabetes
aliases: allogeneic pancreatic islet transplantation in T1D
islet cell transplantation for type 1 diabetes
new_entities.description: Allogeneic pancreatic islet transplantation used in selected people with type 1 diabetes, especially those with severe hypoglycemia or brittle glycemic control.

new_entities.name: Insulin independence
new_entities.description: Ability to remain off exogenous insulin while maintaining meaningful graft function and adequate glycemic control.

edges.effect_quant: Islet transplantation can achieve insulin independence in a substantial minority of carefully selected patients, but durability is limited. In the Edmonton international trial, 44% met the primary insulin-independence endpoint at 1 year and only 31% of initial responders remained insulin-independent at 2 years; a 10-year cohort found 39% insulin independence at 5 years and 28% at 10 years, while another 10-year network reported only 4.8% independence at 10 years despite durable hypoglycemia benefits.
edges.population: adults with type 1 diabetes selected for allogeneic islet transplantation, often because of severe hypoglycemia, glycemic instability, or prior kidney transplantation
edges.mechanism: Transplanted islets can restore endogenous insulin secretion and improve glucose stability, but long-term independence is threatened by graft attrition, alloimmunity, recurrence of autoimmunity, and immunosuppression-related constraints.
edges.summary: This is genuinely mixed. Early and medium-term insulin independence is achievable, but the long-term curve falls off, so the therapy is better understood as a way to improve metabolic stability and severe hypoglycemia rather than a reliably durable cure.
edges.caveats: Outcomes are highly center-dependent and apply to carefully selected patients under specialized protocols. Long-term graft function can persist even when insulin independence is lost, so this edge should not be interpreted as the full value proposition of islet transplantation.

evidence.citation: ShapiroAMJ et al 2006 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: International trial of the Edmonton protocol for islet transplantation.

effect_quant.comparator: participants meeting the primary endpoint of insulin independence with adequate glycemic control 1 year after final transplantation
